prompt: Joana's first mapping was written from Coleta's documentation. Why does a migration profile the data before writing the mapping?
hint: Think of the municipality field and the binder.

choices.text: To find out how many servers and how much disk the load will need
choices.why: Volumes help size the load, but that is not why profiling comes first; the binder was wrong about what the field held, not about its size.

choices.text: Because the new system refuses any load that has not been profiled first
choices.why: No system asks for that. Profiling is a decision the migration team makes so that surprises arrive early.

choices.text: So that the business owners have a report to sign before the project starts
choices.why: Owners sign the mapping specification and the reconciliation. The profile is a measurement, not a document for signature.

choices.text: The binder describes intent, and the data has drifted from it
choices.why: Right: the binder said the municipality came from a list, and the profile found 97 spellings of 38 towns.

prompt: The profile finds 38 tax ids that each appear on two farm records. What should the migration do with them?
hint: Is a shared tax id the same thing as a duplicate farm?

choices.text: Ask somebody who knows the farms which pairs are one tank twice, and merge only those
choices.why: Right: 31 pairs were one producer with two properties, and only 7 were one tank registered twice. Sebastião knew which.

choices.text: Merge each pair into one farm, since a tax id identifies one producer
choices.why: That merges 31 producers' second properties and pays each of them once instead of twice.

choices.text: Add a unique constraint on tax id in the new system so the duplicates cannot load
choices.why: The constraint would refuse 31 correct farms. The rule the binder implied is not true of the data.

choices.text: Send all 76 records to the reject file, for finance to sort out with the producers after go-live
choices.why: Those farms would have no record in the new system, and a farm with no record is a farm that is not paid.

prompt: Coleta's farm master holds 2,140 records. 182 of them have no collection inside the period the new system must hold. How many farms are in scope for the migration?
hint: A subtraction.

prompt: Which of these profiling findings would have loaded without any error, and been found only by a farm paid into a closed account?
hint: A load fails on a value that breaks a rule.

choices.text: Municipalities typed as free text, in 97 spellings
choices.why: These would fail: the new system stores an IBGE code, and an unknown spelling has none.

choices.text: Collection rows pointing at six deleted farm codes
choices.why: Orphans fail loudly too, since the new history needs a farm to belong to.

choices.text: Bank accounts kept in Coleta that disagree with SAP's vendor master
choices.why: Right: they are well formed and wrong, which is the kind of value a load accepts and a payment finds.

choices.text: CPFs whose check digits do not add up
choices.why: The mapping refuses a CPF whose check digits fail, so these surface as rejects, not as payments.

prompt: The new system generates its own farm_id. Why does the mapping also keep Coleta's code in legacy_code?
hint: Who looks things up in Coleta after the cutover?

choices.text: Because the new system cannot generate identifiers that are unique
choices.why: It generates farm_id without trouble. The old code is kept for a different reason.

choices.text: So that Coleta's code can replace farm_id after the hypercare weeks
choices.why: Nothing replaces farm_id. The old code is for looking back, and it is the new id that the new system joins by.

choices.text: Because SAP pays the farms by their Coleta code
choices.why: SAP pays a vendor record, and the mapping carries the vendor number in its own field.

choices.text: So any record leads back to its Coleta farm
choices.why: Right: it costs one column and answers every question about which Coleta farm a record was.

prompt: Finance finds 9 invalid CPFs in Coleta. Joana's first instinct is to correct them in the transformation. Why did Serra Alta correct them in Coleta instead?
hint: What does Coleta keep doing after the farm master moves?

choices.text: Because the transformation cannot change the value of a field
choices.why: It changes plenty: units, spellings, layouts. Whether it can is not the question.

choices.text: Coleta keeps running, so a fact fixed only in flight stays wrong there
choices.why: Right: the strangler keeps Coleta alive for months, and a wrong fact is corrected where it lives.

choices.text: Because corrections in flight are slower than corrections at the source
choices.why: Nine values cost nothing in flight. Speed is not why the place was chosen.

choices.text: Because the owner of a fact is the only person allowed to run the migration
choices.why: Owners sign rules and fix facts; the migration team runs the load.

prompt: Filling a mandatory field nobody can fill with an invented value is dangerous: a ___ is a value somebody will later believe.
hint: The route 1 example.

prompt: Which of these did Serra Alta translate in flight, in the transformation? Choose all that apply.
hint: Wrong forms in flight, wrong facts at the source.

choices.text: The 97 municipality spellings, into IBGE codes
choices.why: Yes: a spelling is a wrong form, translated by a signed table.

choices.text: The 4 farms pointing at blocked SAP vendors
choices.why: A stale link is a wrong fact; finance corrected it in Coleta's own screens.

choices.text: Litres stored as hundredths, into a decimal
choices.why: Yes: a unit is a form, and the rule runs at every load.

choices.text: The 7 farms registered twice, into their survivors
choices.why: Yes: the merge table re-keys them on the way, signed row by row by Sebastião.

prompt: What does a dress rehearsal find that a mock load does not?
hint: Who runs each, when, and on how much data?

choices.text: A spelling the municipality table does not know
choices.why: A mock load finds that; it is a mapping fault, and mock loads exist to test the mapping.

choices.text: Rejected rows, grouped by the reason for each
choices.why: Every run counts rejects by reason, mock loads included.

choices.text: A step that takes hours on full volume, at night
choices.why: Right: only the whole runbook, at the real hours, on a full copy, shows the night as it will be.

choices.text: Whether the mapping specification has been signed
choices.why: That is a document check before any run, not something a rehearsal discovers.

prompt: The cutover window runs from Saturday 20:00 to Sunday 10:00, and the rehearsed rollback takes 2 hours. How many hours after the 20:00 freeze is the latest moment to take the go/no-go decision?
hint: The window's length, less the rollback.

prompt: Dress rehearsal 1 rejected 41 of the 1,958 farms in scope. What percentage of the farms was rejected? Give two decimal places.
hint: Rejects divided by the farms in scope, times 100.

prompt: Dress rehearsal 1 rejected 2,412 collection rows because their lab results were empty. What was wrong?
hint: What does Serra Alta do when a sample is lost?

choices.text: The rows: the lab results had been deleted in Coleta
choices.why: Nothing was deleted. The samples were lost or spoiled, and the rows record that truthfully.

choices.text: The specification: a mandatory field the business leaves empty for a reason
choices.why: Right: a lost sample is paid at the base price, so the rule became optional with a reason code, signed by Cláudia.

choices.text: The load: it ran out of time before the lab results arrived
choices.why: The duration problem was real but separate; these rows were refused by a rule, not by the clock.

choices.text: The extract: it read the history before the lab files were merged in
choices.why: The extract was complete. The emptiness was in Coleta, on purpose.

prompt: Edson's first dress rehearsal for the move off SAP ECC overruns its weekend window by six hours. Following the reasoning of this lesson, which change should he look at first?
hint: What cannot change any more, and so can move early?

choices.text: Skip the record-level reconciliation of the history
choices.why: That buys time by removing the only check that saw Serra Alta's 214 swapped rows.

choices.text: Load the documents of closed periods days before the window opens
choices.why: Right: a closed period will not change, so it can move and be reconciled before the night, as Serra Alta's paid months did.

choices.text: Stop rehearsing the rollback, since it takes time from the run
choices.why: The rollback's measured time is what sets the latest decision; without it the plan has a guess in it.

choices.text: Ask finance to give him the first week of the month as well
choices.why: That is the close week, when the SAP team freezes changes; it is the one week the calendar cannot give.

prompt: Match each check to the fault it is the first to catch.
hint: Count, total, record, then a person.

pairs.right: a row dropped during the load
litres divided by 100 one time too many
two farms that exchanged their litres
fat loaded into the protein field by the spec

right_distractors: a load that overruns its window

prompt: 1,958 farms are in scope, nothing is rejected, and 7 duplicate farms are merged into their survivors on purpose. How many farms should the reconciliation expect in the target?
hint: Every source row is loaded, rejected or merged.

prompt: Run on target-faulty.csv, reconcile.py prints ok for the count and for the litres, then names four farms. How can both totals agree while four farms are wrong?
hint: Look at what each of the faults does to the two sums.

choices.text: The program rounds the litres before it adds them up
choices.why: It refuses to round: a value with a third decimal stops the run.

choices.text: The count and the total are computed from the source file alone
choices.why: Each side is read separately; the output prints both, source and target.

choices.text: Four faults are below the tolerance the first two levels allow
choices.why: There is no tolerance: the levels compare for equality, and here they really are equal.

choices.text: A swap and a mistyped code each leave both sums unchanged
choices.why: Right: two farms exchanging litres keep the total, and one farm under the wrong code keeps both the count and the litres.

prompt: To save time on the night, Rui proposes reconciling the files the transformation read against the tables the load wrote. What is wrong with that?
hint: Compare the ends, not the middle.

choices.text: It proves only that the load agrees with itself
choices.why: Right: the source should come from Coleta at the freeze and the target from the new system as users see it.

choices.text: Staging files are too large to fingerprint in one night
choices.why: Size is not the issue; what the comparison can prove is.

choices.text: A reconciliation is only allowed to read data through an API
choices.why: There is no such rule. Reading the target as users see it is the point, whatever the channel.

choices.text: The staging files hold the rows that were rejected
choices.why: Rejects have their own files, and the reconciliation counts them on purpose.

prompt: Put these steps of Serra Alta's cutover runbook in order.
hint: From Coleta's last file to the readings the trucks held.
items: Coleta writes its last nightly file for SAP
trap: Releasing the held readings before the decision would put real data into a system that may still be rolled back.

prompt: Why are the go/no-go criteria written weeks before the cutover night?
hint: Who is in the room at five in the morning?

choices.text: Because at five in the morning everyone in the room wants a yes
choices.why: Right: written in advance, the question is only whether each line is true.

choices.text: Because the auditors require them for the FSSC 22000 certification
choices.why: That audit is about food safety, not about migrations.

choices.text: Because the runbook cannot be printed until the criteria are in it
choices.why: Printing is not the reason; the meeting would be just as weak with them on a screen.

choices.text: So that the decision can be taken by Rui's team without Regina
choices.why: Regina takes it, with Marcos. Writing the criteria early does not move the decision to somebody else.

prompt: At what moment did Serra Alta's migration reach its point of no return?
hint: After it, going back would mean asking farms for money.

choices.text: At the freeze, when Coleta became read-only for everybody
choices.why: Unfreezing Coleta is the first step of the rehearsed two-hour rollback, so nothing is final yet.

choices.text: At the go decision, at 05:00 on Sunday
choices.why: After the go, going back costs more each day, but the readings can still be carried back to Coleta.

choices.text: When the bank file of the first new payment leaves
choices.why: Right: once farms are paid from the new system, undoing it means reversing payments to about 1,900 farms.

choices.text: When the window closes, at 10:00 on Sunday
choices.why: The window's end limits the night's rollback, not every way back; a fallback exists for days after it.

prompt: To give the new system more time before its first payment, Regina suggests moving the cutover to the first Saturday of the month. Which objection follows from Serra Alta's calendar?
hint: What happens in the first five working days?

choices.text: The trucks do not collect on the first weekend of the month
choices.why: The trucks collect every day of the year; there is no quiet weekend.

choices.text: SAP is in maintenance for the whole of that weekend
choices.why: SAP's maintenance is every Sunday from 01:00 to 05:00, the same in every week.

choices.text: The first payment would then fall inside the cutover window
choices.why: The payment is on the 10th and the window is one night; they cannot overlap from that date.

choices.text: It is the close week, and SAP changes are frozen
choices.why: Right: the first week was out for that reason, so the window sits after the 10th.

prompt: Why did Serra Alta keep Coleta running read-only for twelve months instead of switching it off after the cutover?
hint: A farm disputes July's payment in September.

choices.text: So the trucks could fall back to it if the new system stopped
choices.why: Read-only means nothing can be recorded in it; it cannot take readings.

choices.text: To answer disputes about the months it paid
choices.why: Right: it answers questions about the past without migrating all of it, and legacy_code joins the two.

choices.text: Because the IBM i licence could not be cancelled before then
choices.why: The lesson treats the licence as the cost of the decision, not its reason.

choices.text: So that its nightly file to SAP could keep running in parallel
choices.why: After the cutover the new system writes that file; two files would double every goods receipt.

prompt: Three farms with exactly 3.50% fat were put in the wrong quality band by the new system. Why did no reconciliation catch it?
hint: What does a reconciliation compare?

choices.text: The values arrived intact; the fault was a rule using them
choices.why: Right: the lab results were migrated correctly; a band boundary is a rule, found only by using the data.

choices.text: Because the owner's sample of 40 farms was too small
choices.why: The sample looks for a wrong mapping rule; the payment rules are not in the mapping at all.

choices.text: Because fingerprints ignore decimals in the lab results
choices.why: A fingerprint covers every field in the agreed form, decimals included.

choices.text: Because the control total was taken on litres and not on fat
choices.why: A total on fat would have agreed too: the fat values arrived intact.

prompt: Which archive of Coleta's old data follows the lesson?
hint: It has to open in twenty years, after its author has retired.

choices.text: A full backup of the IBM i, kept with no end date in case it is needed
choices.why: It needs an IBM i to restore, and an archive with no end date is a cost and a liability kept forever.

choices.text: The history migrated into the new system as well, so there is one place to look
choices.why: The scope rule kept old history out of the new system on purpose; moving it all would undo that decision.

choices.text: Plain CSV with a description of each field, an owner, and a disposal date
choices.why: Right: it opens anywhere, explains itself after Sebastião leaves, and ends on a written date.

choices.text: Coleta's database tables exported unchanged, without any documentation
choices.why: Without the field descriptions, the meaning leaves with the RPG and its author.

prompt: At 05:00 the reconciliation shows 1,951 farms, matching litres, and 3 changed records that are not on the list of expected changes. Both samples are signed. Which statements follow from the lesson? Choose all that apply.
hint: Read the criteria one by one.

choices.text: The answer is no-go unless the three are explained by a rule
choices.why: Yes: a difference with no rule behind it stops the cutover.

choices.text: The answer is go, since the count and the litres both match
choices.why: Those two levels let through exactly the faults the third one exists for.

choices.text: Whatever is decided has to be decided by 08:00
choices.why: Yes: the window ends at 10:00 and the rollback needs two hours.

choices.text: The team may add the three to the expected list to keep the date
choices.why: That is a criterion bent on the night; an expected change has a rule written before it.

prompt: In a rehearsal, 1,958 farms are in scope, 7 are merged on purpose, and the target holds 1,948 farms. How many farms must the reject file account for, if the farm master reconciles?
hint: Source rows = target rows + rejected + merged.

prompt: A colleague migrating Salesforce accounts into Business Central says: the load finished without an error, so we are done. Which reply sums up this lesson?
hint: What has a load without errors proved?

choices.text: Done, once the old system is switched off the same weekend
choices.why: Switching off the old system on the day removes the place where every question about the past is answered.

choices.text: Only that nothing it checked went wrong
choices.why: Right: values wrong but well formed load silently, and some faults only show when the business uses the data.

choices.text: Done, if the row counts on both sides are the same
choices.why: A count is the first of three levels; it cannot see a row that arrived with the wrong value.

choices.text: Not yet: run the same load again to see it is repeatable
choices.why: A second clean run proves the load agrees with itself twice, which says nothing about the target being right.
